page.layout: One page of verse, one column, with a running head at the top and a closing line and signature at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.p: In Christi media domo, intimisque Sanctorum penetralibus, (quid addam?) Fortunis opibusque caterorum Partis non sine maximo labore, Ordo hic nascitur oppido beatus.
Dulces deinde fauos suo venenô Veram Euangelij & salubriorem Doctrinam inficit, atque in vniuersum Christi corpus vt inuehat malorum Errorum illuuiem, nocensque virus, Velis nititur omnibusq; remis.

Tum ne sit similis parum Pyrausta, Vndecunque sibi parárit alas, E caecis tenebris, meráque nocte, Quam ignorantia veritatis infert, Non cessat, neque definet profectlo[?], Sacrum Euangelij inuolare lumen, Donec iudicij igne adustus ille Diuini cadat occidatque totus.
Hac autem ratione constituta, Quid restat, nisi clericos vt istos, Qui Papam studio sequuntur omni Doctrinae caput Antichristianae, Agnoscas merito suo notari.
Quin mentem decet vt piam deinceps Papae & Papilionibus precemur.

page.notes: The closing line "P. S. I. C," is set in the main text as a sigla line. The reading "profectlo" is uncertain; the printed word may be "profectio". The signature "H. iij." is at the foot right. The faint mirrored text on the right side of the scan is show-through and was left out.
